/-!
# Erdős Problem 705

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/705](https://www.erdosproblems.com/705)
- [OD99] P. O'Donnell, High girth unit-distance graphs. PhD Dissertation, Rutgers University (1999).
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos705

open scoped EuclideanGeometry
open SimpleGraph

/--
Let $G$ be a finite unit distance graph in $\mamthbb{R}^2$.
Is there some $k$ such that if $G$ has girth $≥ k$, then $\chi(G) ≤ 3$?

The general case was solved by O'Donnell [OD99], who constructed finite unit distance graphs with
chromatic number $4$ and arbitrarily large girth.
-/

reformulations.difference: The statement uses Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.girth : ℕ`, which is `0` for acyclic graphs. So for k ≥ 1 a forest does not satisfy `girth ≥ k`. In the source, a forest has 'girth ≥ k (i.e. G contains no cycles of length < k)' for every k.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Forests are 2-colourable (`IsAcyclic.colorable_two`), so they satisfy the conclusion χ ≤ 3 either way. A graph with a cycle has `girth = egirth.toNat` equal to the length of a shortest cycle (`exists_egirth_eq_length`), so `girth ≥ k` holds exactly when every cycle has length ≥ k. Conversely, `girth ≥ k` gives k ≤ the length of every cycle (`girth_le_length`). So for each fixed k and each finite V, the Lean implication and the source's implication have the same truth value, and the two ∃k statements coincide. Hence `False ↔ RHS` is exactly the source's negative answer. Proved in a scratch file importing the module: `(∃ k, ∀ V : Set ℝ², V.Finite → (UnitDistancePlaneGraph V).girth ≥ k → χ ≤ 3) ↔ (∃ k : ℕ, ∀ V : Set ℝ², V.Finite → (∀ (a : V) (w : (UnitDistancePlaneGraph V).Walk a a), w.IsCycle → k ≤ w.length) → χ ≤ 3)`, together with the corollary `(False ↔ LeanRHS) ↔ ¬ SourceRHS`. Both compile and use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

review.notes:
I found no findings; the file is correct. What I checked:

(1) The source explicitly uses the faithful/induced unit-distance graph: an edge between two points if and only if their distance is 1. `SimpleGraph.UnitDistancePlaneGraph` is literally this, on `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)` with the L2 distance. I confirmed in Lean that (0,0) and (3/5,4/5) are adjacent and that the graph has no loops.

(2) The forum records a debate over whether O'Donnell's construction is faithful. The cited formal proof (plby/lean-proofs @8822f7dd, line 8323, `not_erdos_705`) addresses this. It uses the same graph definition and proves `¬ ∃ k, ∀ V : Set ℝ², V.Finite → girth ≥ k → χ ≤ 3`, including an explicit generic-perturbation argument that rules out accidental unit distances between non-adjacent vertices. So `answer(False)`, `research solved` and the formal_proof record all match the source ('DISPROVED', page last edited 27 Jan 2026). There are no status issues.

(3) Erdős's original wording ([Er81, p.27]): 'Let S be a subset of the plane. Join two points of S if their distance is 1 and assume that the resulting graph G(S) has girth k. Denote by χ_k(E²) the maximum value of the chromatic number of G(S). Is there a k for which χ_k(E²) = 3?' This is equivalent to the erdosproblems.com version (finite, girth ≥ k, χ ≤ 3), which the Lean follows. The de Bruijn–Erdős theorem reduces arbitrary S to finite subsets, since induced subgraphs do not decrease girth. Also χ_k ≥ 3 always, because regular odd polygons with unit sides have χ = 3 and arbitrarily large girth.

(4) Cosmetic docstring typo, not reported as a finding: `$\mamthbb{R}^2$` should be `$\mathbb{R}^2$` in the theorem docstring.

(5) Access note: erdosproblems.com returned a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' challenge to curl with several descriptive User-Agents, and web.archive.org and archive.ph were unreachable or blocked. I read the page, its LaTeX view and its forum thread through the r.jina.ai reader proxy.
